title: Quantum entanglement within quarkonium
authors: Wenyu Zhang, Yiyu Zhou, Yang Li, Qun Wang
abstract: We investigate quark-antiquark entanglement in heavy quarkonium within a nonperturbative light-front Hamiltonian framework. By tracing over the antiquark degrees of freedom in the hadronic state vector, we construct the reduced density matrix of the quark subsystem and compute the associated von Neumann entropy. For spin-0 quarkonia, we show that this entropy reduces to the Shannon entropy of the unpolarized transverse momentum dependent parton distribution (TMD), up to constant color and spin contributions. For spin-1 quarkonia, we derive the explicit polarization dependence of the entropy and connect it to polarized and tensor-polarized TMDs. Using light-front wave functions obtained via basis light-front quantization (BLFQ), we evaluate the entanglement entropy for charmonium and bottomonium states, revealing a pronounced sensitivity to the polarization of vector mesons. Furthermore, we resolve the infrared parameter by matching the momentum-space entropy to a harmonic-oscillator representation. Ultimately, these results establish entanglement entropy as a novel probe of nonperturbative quarkonium structure, forging a direct link between quantum information measures and partonic observables.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the entanglement entropy within heavy quarkonium states ($	ext{charmonium}$ and $	ext{bottomonium}$) using a light-front Hamiltonian approach. It establishes that this quantum information measure provides a direct, quantitative link between fundamental quantum correlations and measurable partonic structure functions (TMDs). The results demonstrate how polarization affects the entanglement, offering a powerful new tool for probing nonperturbative QCD.
main_problem: The study investigates quantifying quantum entanglement within heavy quarkonium bound states ($	ext{charmonium}$ and $	ext{bottomonium}$) to probe their nonperturbative internal structure.
main_result: Entanglement entropy ($S_q$) is shown to be a novel observable that directly links quantum information measures to measurable partonic observables, such as transverse momentum dependent parton distributions (TMDs).
method: The authors employ the von Neumann entropy calculation on the reduced density matrix ($ho_q$), derived within a nonperturbative light-front Hamiltonian framework using Basis Light-Front Quantization (BLFQ).
model_or_system: The system is heavy quarkonium ($q ar{q}$), modeled using an effective Hamiltonian solved via the light-front Schrödinger equation. Calculations are performed in the valence Fock sector, utilizing Gaussian wavepackets and taking the Narrow Wavepacket Limit ($\sigma 	o 0$).
key_observables: Entanglement entropy ($S_q$), reduced density matrix ($ho_q$), and various TMDs (unpolarized $f_1$, polarized $h_\perp^1$, etc.).
important_parameters: Polarization of the vector mesons, infrared cutoffs ($\Lambda_{	ext{IR}}$), and the wavepacket width parameter $\sigma$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on retaining only the valence Fock sector and taking the Narrow Wavepacket Limit ($\sigma 	o 0$) to simplify the density matrix diagonalization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates 3D images of unpolarized TMDs for various charmonium states. Figure 2 shows 3D images of eigenvalues related to these TMDs for different quarkonium spin states.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by defining entanglement entropy in the light-front framework, deriving specific formulas for spin-0 and spin-1 mesons connecting $S_q$ to TMDs, evaluating these quantities for charmonium/bottomonium, and finally proposing a method to resolve infrared divergences.
why_interesting: While focused on QCD structure rather than AMO systems, the methodology of using entanglement entropy as a diagnostic tool is highly relevant. The techniques developed for handling reduced density matrices in strongly coupled field theories could inspire analogous studies in open quantum systems or many-body physics where correlations are key.
